source.title: Exemplary Natural Images Explain CNN Activations Better than Feature Visualizations
source.authors: Judy Borowski; R. Zimmermann; Judith Schepers; Robert Geirhos; Thomas S. A. Wallis; M. Bethge; Wieland Brendel

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates how well people predict InceptionV1 feature-map activations from reference images. It does not test whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs or any other listed version of the polysemanticity claim.
record.gate_note: The paper mentions polysemantic units as background, but reports no measurements of neuron polysemanticity. The recorded results concern the related, distinct measure of human prediction accuracy for feature-map activations.
record.test_reason: The study measures how well humans predict which natural image strongly activates InceptionV1 feature maps, given synthetic or natural reference images. It mentions polysemantic units only as background (citing Zoom In). It reports no rate or measure of neurons responding to unrelated inputs, no superposition, architecture or measurement analysis, so it tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Synthetic visualizations help humans predict InceptionV1 feature-map activations, but natural exemplars are substantially more informative across layers, expertise levels and selection modes. The authors caution that the setup is designed for maximal performance and probes only one task. Note also that the abstract reports 65±5% for synthetic Max 1, while Section 4.5 reports 64±5%.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a human forward-prediction task comparing Olah et al. feature visualizations with natural images; it does not reproduce a method for identifying or testing polysemantic neurons.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction accuracy varied with reference-image presentation; the authors report that additional reference information improved performance, especially for natural images.

fits_no_version.finding: Humans predict strongly activating InceptionV1 feature-map images above chance with synthetic feature visualizations (82±4%), better with natural exemplars (92±2%); in Max 1, 64±5% vs 73±4%; in Min+Max 9, 72±4% vs 91±3%. No-reference condition is near chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Exemplary natural images let humans predict CNN feature-map activations better than Olah et al. (2017) synthetic feature visualizations.

record.problems: The study tests one Inception V1 network and one feature-visualization method. Its task and design choices aim to maximize participant performance; the authors note this may not represent less optimal setups or other applications. The experiments use 10 participants in Experiment I and 23 in Experiment II.
record.rows_left_out: Confidence, reaction-time, subjective intuitiveness, and additional layer/branch analyses are not included because they do not measure neuron polysemanticity or the recorded feature-map prediction accuracy rows.

untested.parts: Whether InceptionV1 neurons respond to several unrelated inputs; feature maps are studied only for human predictability, not polysemanticity.
No architecture or activation-function comparison; one network only.
No reinterpretation of polysemantic neurons as one shared feature.
Uses only extreme activation tails; no comparison of polysemanticity across activation ranges or scoring methods.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': polysemanticity appears only in one introductory sentence citing Olah et al. 2020b. The by-feature-map analysis notes that difficult maps have diverse reference images. This is a qualitative remark about human difficulty, not a measure of polysemanticity, so no row or missing entry is warranted. Rows correctly carry versions ['none'] and state cannot_determine.

versions.untested_parts: Whether individual image-classifier neurons respond to several unrelated inputs.
Language models, MLP neurons, unrelated tokens or contexts, and layer differences.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
Polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise without capacity pressure.
Effects of activation function, architecture, or regularization on polysemanticity and performance.
Whether apparently unrelated neuron responses share a coherent feature or job.
Whether classifying neurons as polysemantic depends on activation range or explanation scoring.

rows.subject: human participants (Experiment I aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Participants chose which of two natural query images strongly activated an InceptionV1 feature map, given synthetic reference images.
rows.note: Aggregate participant accuracy for the forward-prediction task; the measure does not assess neuron polysemanticity.

rows.subject: human participants (Experiment I aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Participants chose which of two natural query images strongly activated an InceptionV1 feature map, given natural reference images.
rows.note: Aggregate participant accuracy; the authors report natural references outperform synthetic references.

rows.subject: human participants (Experiment I aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Participants chose which of two natural query images strongly activated an InceptionV1 feature map without reference images.
rows.note: The paper does not give an exact accuracy for this condition.

rows.subject: human participants (Experiment II aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Participants chose which of two natural query images strongly activated an InceptionV1 feature map, given one maximally activating synthetic reference image.
rows.note: Aggregate accuracy in the single-maximally-activating-reference condition; this does not measure polysemanticity.

rows.subject: human participants (Experiment II aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Participants chose which of two natural query images strongly activated an InceptionV1 feature map, given one maximally activating natural reference image.
rows.note: Aggregate accuracy; natural references outperform synthetic references in this condition.

rows.subject: human participants (Experiment II aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Participants chose which of two natural query images strongly activated an InceptionV1 feature map, given nine maximally and minimally activating synthetic reference images.
rows.note: Aggregate accuracy in the condition the authors describe as a replication of Experiment I.

rows.subject: human participants (Experiment II aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Participants chose which of two natural query images strongly activated an InceptionV1 feature map, given nine maximally and minimally activating natural reference images.
rows.note: Aggregate accuracy; natural references outperform synthetic references in this condition.
